blocks.basis: seven players are the European powers on a map of Europe before the First World War
players hold home supply centres and the game ends when one player controls 18 of the 34
each year has four phases, two for talking and settling orders and two for carrying the orders out
players collect coloured cards, use them to place train pieces on routes joining cities, and score points
a piece landing on a space held by an opponent sends the occupier back to the start and costs it a counter
the creek space sweeps a piece that lands there back to the start and costs it a counter
progress round the board is a means to gather counters, and the side that wins all the counters conquers
players reason about the unseen tiles on the opponent's rack from the plays they have made

a player who plays a phony word that is successfully challenged retracts it and loses the turn, so play runs in turns
each side tries to advance all fifteen pieces to the finish line and off the board using dice
in the reconstruction, a lone piece captured by the opponent has to re-enter from the first row
the paper calls these chance-based racing games played by throwing dice
